short: Scalogram CNNs (M06) and ImageNet weights (M03) were new for imagined speech but are standard: effects not isolated, and pre-stimulus decoding at 42.96% inflates every stage.
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06) to Morlet scalograms, per sensor or as a 14 × 14 sensor mosaic, classified by CNNs, and training (M03) to ImageNet initialisation [@dash2020decoding]. None of the 17 earlier imagined-speech decoders of any electrophysiological signal used either (Appendix), but both are standard: the only comparator is a shallow network with more inputs than training trials, the mosaic's gain is not significant in the imagination stage and coincides with augmentation used only for the mosaic, and no network is trained from scratch. Evaluation (M12) follows the usual within-subject trial split; its own pre-stimulus control is classified at 42.96% against the authors' 30% chance (Table 1). The same laboratory's later study on the same paradigm and RMS features reports 45.46% for imagined phrases under 5-fold cross-validation [@dash2020sensor], against 80.83% for the shallow network here, so the 93% imagined-phrase figure describes a within-session protocol for a preparation interval after reading, not decodable imagined speech.
